name: Lizzie Fletcher
signature: Houston Democrat on Energy and Commerce who signed the 81-member letter against a state AI-law moratorium and is an original cosponsor of the GUARDRAILS Act; quiet on data centers.

notable_quote.text: strong opposition to any effort in the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) that would reintroduce a sweeping moratorium on the ability of states and local governments to enforce their own artificial intelligence (AI) laws and regulations

data_centers.summary: No public position found on AI data centers as of Sept 2026. She sits on the Energy and Commerce Energy Subcommittee that heard the data center cost bills in April 2026, but the only remark attributed to her there was about the scope of a transmission-rates bill, and she has not cosponsored the Ratepayer Protection Act.

evidence.title: Hearing summary: House Energy Subcommittee hears bipartisan agreement on data center cost allocation (Daily Energy Insider)
evidence.what_it_shows: At the April 29, 2026 Energy Subcommittee hearing on seven data-center and grid bills, the summary records Fletcher only questioning the breadth of the FAIR Act's covered-policy definition, not taking a position on data centers or ratepayer bills.

ai_risk.summary: Her only AI-safety record is cosponsoring the 2024 bill to make sharing AI-made sexual deepfakes illegal. No speeches, letters or interviews on advanced AI dangers were found.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Preventing Deepfakes of Intimate Images Act (118th, H.R. 3106)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed a targeted rule against AI-generated intimate deepfakes, a specific guardrail rather than broad AI regulation.

tech_regulation.summary: Repeatedly backs targeted privacy rules for sensitive health data. She cosponsored the My Body, My Data Act in 2023 and the Reproductive Data Privacy and Protection Act in September 2026. No broader Big Tech or Section 230 stance found.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Reproductive Data Privacy and Protection Act (H.R. 3218)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports stopping companies from collecting or selling reproductive health data without permission.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: My Body, My Data Act of 2023 (118th, H.R. 3420)
evidence.what_it_shows: Earlier support for the same targeted health-data privacy protections.

evidence.title: Transcript: House E&C hearing on a proposal to sunset Section 230 (Tech Policy Press)
evidence.what_it_shows: At the Section 230 sunset hearing she focused on reproductive-health speech and asked how Section 230 works as an immunity from suit, without endorsing repeal.

preemption.summary: Clearly wants states to keep their power to regulate AI. She signed the November 2025 letter from 81 House Democrats opposing a state AI-law moratorium and the planned executive order, and she was an original cosponsor of the GUARDRAILS Act to repeal the White House preemption push.

evidence.title: Letter: 81 House Democrats led by Rep. Matsui oppose an AI moratorium in the NDAA and the planned preemption executive order
evidence.quote: strong opposition to any effort in the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) that would reintroduce a sweeping moratorium on the ability of states and local governments to enforce their own artificial intelligence (AI) laws and regulations
evidence.what_it_shows: Fletcher's name appears among the signers; the letter argues states must be free to enforce their own AI laws and notes the Senate rejected the moratorium 99-1.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: GUARDRAILS Act (H.R. 8031)
evidence.what_it_shows: Joined the bill to block the federal government from wiping out state AI laws on the day it was introduced.

evidence.title: Press release: Jacobs, Beyer, Matsui, Lieu, McClain Delaney introduce legislation to repeal White House AI moratorium
evidence.what_it_shows: Lists Lizzie Fletcher (D-TX) among the original House cosponsors of the GUARDRAILS Act, confirming she signed on at introduction.

china_chips.summary: No public statements, votes or bills found on chip export controls or Nvidia sales to China as of Sept 2026.

search_notes: Searches: 'Lizzie Fletcher artificial intelligence', 'Lizzie Fletcher data center', 'Fletcher Energy and Commerce AI/data centers electricity', 'Lizzie Fletcher chatbot/deepfake/Big Tech/Section 230', 'Fletcher Ratepayer Protection Act', 'Lizzie Fletcher KOSA/privacy/TikTok', 'Congresswoman Fletcher AI', plus fletcher.house.gov press release pages 1-6 (Dec 2025 to June 2026) and her 2025 annual report. Verified the Matsui letter signature by extracting the PDF text (Fletcher present; Al Green absent). Verified GUARDRAILS original cosponsorship in the Jacobs release. She did not sign the Dec 3, 2025 Clarke letter or the Aug 10, 2026 Casar letter on AI CEO hearings (grepped both). Govtrack shows she is not a cosponsor of H.R. 9340 Ratepayer Protection Act as of Sept 12, 2026. Tech Policy Press transcripts of the Nov 2025 chatbot hearing and Apr 2025 AI-energy hearing do not include her. The Daily Energy Insider hearing summary was read via the r.jina.ai proxy (direct fetch blocked), so her FAIR Act remark is described, not quoted. Wayback Machine and Google News link decoding were unavailable for most of the session.

name: Morgan Luttrell
signature: Former Navy SEAL who helped set up the Energy Department's AI office; focuses on cyber threats and AI at the border, favors industry-led innovation, no stated view on AI rules.

notable_quote.text: If we move to a point where artificial intelligence removes the human element, but you needed the human element to (discover the attack), what happens?

data_centers.summary: No public statements or bills found on AI data centers, electricity bills or ratepayers as of Sept 2026. His energy issues page covers oil reserves and grid grants, not data centers.

ai_risk.summary: Treats AI mainly as a national security tool and a race with China. In a 2024 op-ed he said industry should lead with government supporting, not stifling, innovation, and he backs using AI at the border. At a December 2025 hearing he did press Anthropic on what happens when AI removes human oversight, but he has proposed no AI rules.

evidence.title: Op-ed: Luttrell, A Bird's Eye View of Cybersecurity (Huntsville Item, reposted on his site)
evidence.quote: we need a strong partnership between the public and private sectors, with industry leading the way and government supporting, not stifling, innovation.
evidence.what_it_shows: Citing his experience standing up the Energy Department's Artificial Intelligence and Technology Office, he frames AI and cyber as a race against China and Russia where industry should lead.

evidence.title: IAPP report: House Homeland Security subcommittees explore cybersecurity implications of AI and quantum computing
evidence.quote: If we move to a point where artificial intelligence removes the human element, but you needed the human element to (discover the attack), what happens?
evidence.what_it_shows: At the Dec 17, 2025 joint hearing on the Anthropic Claude cyberattack report, he questioned the risk of AI automating tasks humans use to catch attacks, showing risk awareness without proposing rules.

evidence.title: Press release: House passes Luttrell, Correa bipartisan Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act
evidence.quote: requiring the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to submit a plan to Congress on integrating cutting-edge technologies, such as artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, and nanotechnology at the border
evidence.what_it_shows: He co-led a bill to expand government use of AI at the border, a pro-adoption stance.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act (H.R. 993)
evidence.what_it_shows: Formal cosponsorship of the border AI planning bill in the 119th Congress.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act (118th, H.R. 7832)
evidence.what_it_shows: Same bill in the prior Congress.

evidence.title: Press release: Luttrell secures key FY27 NDAA wins in committee
evidence.quote: accelerating critical technologies like hypersonics and autonomous systems
evidence.what_it_shows: Praises the defense bill for speeding up autonomous weapons systems, consistent with a pro-adoption view of AI in defense.

tech_regulation.summary: No public position found on Big Tech, Section 230, kids online safety or privacy laws as of Sept 2026.

preemption.summary: No statements, letters or bills found on federal preemption of state AI laws as of Sept 2026.

china_chips.summary: No statements or bills found on chip export controls or Nvidia sales to China as of Sept 2026, though his cyber writing frames China as the main adversary.

search_notes: Searches: 'Morgan Luttrell artificial intelligence', 'Morgan Luttrell data center', 'Luttrell AI cybersecurity critical infrastructure hearing', 'Morgan Luttrell chatbot/deepfake/Big Tech/China chips' (no results), 'Luttrell Homeland Security AI hearing', 'luttrell.house.gov AI/cyber/technology', 'Luttrell data center Conroe/Montgomery/Magnolia' (nothing), Brave search 'Morgan Luttrell artificial intelligence'; plus luttrell.house.gov press releases (pages 0-2, Jun 2025 to Jul 2026), his energy and national security issues pages, and his committees page. Read the Legis1 June 4, 2026 article on the Homeland AI security hearing (lists him only as a subcommittee member, no quote) and the Homeland Security Committee hearing page. An Economic Times video (May 28, 2026) headlines his 'Is money really the solution?' question at a hearing on cyber threats to state and local governments, but no transcript was available, so it is not used as evidence. The Houston Public Media report on AI super PACs shows American Mission backing Steinmann to succeed him, not spending on Luttrell himself. Google News link decoding and the Wayback Machine were down for most of the session.

name: Al Green
signature: Houston Democrat who cosponsors bills against algorithmic discrimination and AI price gouging and co-led a utility-bill cap; lost his May 2026 runoff after a crypto super PAC spent millions against him.

notable_quote.text: unbought, liberated, unafraid Democrat, unbought by crypto cash.

data_centers.summary: Puts ratepayers first through utility-bill legislation. He was an original cosponsor of the Lowering Utility Bills Act, which caps utility profit margins, and cosponsored the Energy Bills Relief Act. Neither bill is written specifically about data centers and he has made no public statement about them.

evidence.title: Original cosponsor: Lowering Utility Bills Act (H.R. 8568, Casar)
evidence.what_it_shows: Joined at introduction a bill capping the return on equity utilities can charge, introduced amid the Texas data center energy-cost fight (cosponsorship confirmed on GovTrack).

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Energy Bills Relief Act (H.R. 7977, Casten)
evidence.what_it_shows: Second ratepayer-cost bill he backed in spring 2026 (date confirmed on GovTrack).

evidence.title: Texas Tribune: Casar bill aims to lower utility costs by capping profit margins
evidence.quote: lawmakers on the House Subcommittee on Energy took up seven of these bills, each related to artificial intelligence and its impact on the power grid.
evidence.what_it_shows: Places the Lowering Utility Bills Act within the wave of ratepayer bills prompted by AI data center power demand in Texas; Green is not quoted.

ai_risk.summary: Backs targeted guardrails, mostly on discrimination and unfair pricing. He cosponsored the AI Civil Rights Act, two versions of the Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act, the Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act, and earlier bills against AI sexual deepfakes and AI election deception. He also filed a resolution condemning Trump's AI-generated image of himself as Jesus. He also backs a tax break for AI worker training.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025 (H.R. 6356)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning discriminatory AI and requiring companies to test their systems for unfair treatment.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026 (H.R. 7110)
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants agencies to set up civil rights teams to catch biased algorithms; he backed the 2024 version too.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 (H.R. 4640)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning AI-driven personalized prices and wages.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act (118th, H.R. 8858)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed a ban on AI fakes used to trick voters.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Preventing Deepfakes of Intimate Images Act (118th, H.R. 3106)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed making AI sexual deepfakes illegal.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2024 (118th, H.R. 10092)
evidence.what_it_shows: Earlier version of the algorithmic bias bill.

evidence.title: Press release: Congressman Al Green introduces a resolution condemning President Trump's social media post depicting himself as Jesus Christ
evidence.quote: describing it as disrespectful and offensive for using artificial intelligence to depict himself (Donald Trump) in a manner consistent with sacred religious imagery.
evidence.what_it_shows: Objects to a specific AI-generated image; a statement of concern about AI imagery, not a regulatory proposal.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: AI Workforce Training Act (H.R. 7576)
evidence.what_it_shows: Also supports a tax break for businesses that train workers to use AI, showing he is not anti-adoption.

tech_regulation.summary: Supports targeted rules such as the My Body, My Data Act on reproductive health data. He has also spotlighted AI and crypto industry money in politics after a crypto super PAC spent more than $4 million against him.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: My Body, My Data Act of 2023 (118th, H.R. 3420)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed limits on apps and companies collecting reproductive health data.

evidence.title: ICYMI post on his official site: BPR article 'AI, crypto industries could have their hooks in lawmakers during next Congress'
evidence.quote: The BPR Business and Politics article below, titled "AI, crypto industries could have their hooks in lawmakers during next Congress," speaks for itself.
evidence.what_it_shows: Signals distrust of AI and crypto industry influence over Congress.

evidence.title: Texas Tribune: In Democratic runoff, Reps. Al Green and Christian Menefee clash over influence of big money in politics
evidence.quote: unbought, liberated, unafraid Democrat, unbought by crypto cash.
evidence.what_it_shows: Attacked the crypto super PAC Protect Progress (a Fairshake affiliate) for spending over $4 million for his opponent; shows hostility to tech-industry money, not a specific regulatory plan.

preemption.summary: No position found. He did not sign the Nov 2025 Matsui letter or the Dec 2025 Clarke letter against preempting state AI laws, and no statements on the executive order or the March 2026 framework were found.

china_chips.summary: No statements or bills found on chip export controls or Nvidia sales to China as of Sept 2026.

name: Michael T. McCaul
signature: Retiring Foreign Affairs chairman emeritus and AI Caucus leader who is one of the House's strongest chip export-control hawks, cheered the Stargate AI buildout in Texas, and later cosponsored the Ratepayer Protection Act.

notable_quote.text: You know, they steal so much intellectual property from this country, but we don't have to sell it to them. And that's the axiom that led me to introduce the ENFORCE Act.

groups: Congressional Artificial Intelligence Caucus (co-chair per ARI Oct 2024 and his own Jan 2025 statement; listed as member on his 119th Congress committees page)
Congressional High Tech Caucus (co-chair and founder)
House Foreign Affairs Committee (chairman emeritus; chairman 2023-2024)

data_centers.summary: Supports building AI infrastructure but has moved to add ratepayer protections. In January 2025 he said he was thrilled by Trump's Stargate AI investment starting in Texas. In June 2026 he cosponsored the Ratepayer Protection Act to keep data center power costs off household electric bills.

evidence.title: Press release: McCaul praises Trump announcement on AI investment in Texas
evidence.quote: I'm thrilled to see President Trump leveraging the power of American innovation and private sector dollars to supercharge our AI industry, with the first project starting in Texas.
evidence.what_it_shows: Celebrated the Stargate AI data center buildout in Texas as a way to make America an AI superpower.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed the bipartisan bill to stop regular customers' electric bills from rising to pay for power that data centers need (date confirmed on GovTrack).

ai_risk.summary: Frames AI as a race with China that America must win and calls AI the future of warfare. His AI bills fund research and keep AI out of China's hands rather than regulate it at home. No statements found on safety testing, licensing or a pause. Americans for Responsible Innovation named him a 2024 Responsible AI Champion for his export-control work.

evidence.title: Press release: McCaul praises Trump announcement on AI investment in Texas
evidence.quote: we stand ready to help President Trump turn our nation into an AI superpower, out-compete our adversaries, and keep Americans safe.
evidence.what_it_shows: Innovation-first, beat-China framing of AI policy.

evidence.title: Press release: McCaul discusses effort to secure AI supply chains with Under Secretary Helberg (HFAC hearing)
evidence.quote: obviously semiconductors, but [also] AI, which is the future of warfare.
evidence.what_it_shows: Treats AI mainly as a military and geopolitical asset and praised the Pax Silica alliance to accelerate the AI race against China.

evidence.title: Americans for Responsible Innovation: ARI recognizes 2024 Responsible AI Champions
evidence.quote: This year's 2024 Responsible AI Champions include: Sen. Maria Cantwell (D-WA), Sen. Todd Young (R-IN), Rep. Michael McCaul (R-TX), and Rep. Don Beyer (D-VA).
evidence.what_it_shows: A pro-safeguards group honored him for the ENFORCE Act on AI model export controls and the CREATE AI Act, and described him as an AI Caucus co-chair; his AI risk work is about foreign adversaries, not domestic rules.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: CREATE AI Act of 2023 (118th, H.R. 5077)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed a national AI research resource so researchers and students, not just big companies, can build AI.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: GUARD Act (H.R. 5466)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports funding universities to do AI research for the military.

evidence.title: Sponsor: Accelerating Innovation (AI) for Kids with Cancer Act (H.R. 9632)
evidence.what_it_shows: Introduced a bill to coordinate federal use of AI in pediatric cancer research, a pro-adoption measure (confirmed on GovTrack).

tech_regulation.summary: His tech-regulation record is aimed at China-linked apps. He sponsored the 2023 DATA Act to let the President block or punish apps like TikTok that are controlled by China. No position found on Section 230, antitrust or kids online safety bills.

evidence.title: Sponsor: DATA Act (118th, H.R. 1153)
evidence.what_it_shows: Wrote the bill giving the President power to block China-controlled apps such as TikTok over Americans' data.

preemption.summary: No statements, letters or bills found on preempting or protecting state AI laws, the Dec 2025 executive order, or the March 2026 White House framework as of Sept 2026.

china_chips.summary: One of the House's leading chip export-control hawks. He says the U.S. should not sell military-grade AI chips or chipmaking tools to China, criticized Nvidia's earlier chip sales as enabling DeepSeek, cosponsored the AI OVERWATCH Act to let Congress block chip sales, introduced the BIS License Administration Enhancement Act, and wants U.S. data firms cut off from Pentagon work if they help Chinese AI labs.

evidence.title: Press release: McCaul discusses importance of keeping American AI out of the CCP's hands at HFAC hearing 'Winning the AI Arms Race Against the Chinese Communist Party'
evidence.quote: You know, they steal so much intellectual property from this country, but we don't have to sell it to them. And that's the axiom that led me to introduce the ENFORCE Act.
evidence.what_it_shows: Attacked the Nvidia deal to sell chips to China, said Nvidia's earlier sales enabled DeepSeek, and endorsed the chairman's AI OVERWATCH bill.

evidence.title: Press release: McCaul remarks at hearing on semiconductor export controls (Export Control Loopholes: Chipmaking Tools and their Subcomponents)
evidence.quote: I see no reason, first of all, that we should be selling AI military-grade technology chips to China.
evidence.what_it_shows: Also said he is drafting a rule to block any affiliate 50 percent or more owned by a blacklisted Chinese entity, and opposed selling chipmaking tools to China.

evidence.title: Press release: McCaul advocates for stronger export controls at Foreign Affairs Committee markup (BIS License Administration Enhancement Act and MATCH Act)
evidence.quote: When it comes to the most sensitive technologies, like high-end chips driving the AI revolution, we cannot just hope our export controls are working. Congress must verify it.
evidence.what_it_shows: Pushed his own bill for a presumption of denial on sensitive tech exports and backed the MATCH Act to force allies to match U.S. chip-tool controls.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: AI OVERWATCH Act (H.R. 6875)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports giving Congress power to block advanced AI chip sales to China before they happen.

evidence.title: Sponsor: Bureau of Industry and Security License Administration Enhancement Act (H.R. 8284)
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill to make private 'is informed' export letters public rules, add national security experts to advisory boards, and require reports on chip rules.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 (H.R. 8283)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs punishing foreign companies, especially in China, that steal or copy American AI models.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: bill to increase civil penalties under the Export Control Reform Act (H.R. 5853)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports much larger fines for companies that break export rules.

evidence.title: New York Post (reposted on Free Republic): Top US data companies supplying data to Chinese AI while also working for Pentagon, GOP rep warns
evidence.quote: We cannot spend billions trying to protect our technological advantage while American companies package up our best human expertise and sell it to companies tied to the Chinese military.
evidence.what_it_shows: Told the Post that U.S. AI data-labeling firms working for Chinese AI labs should not get government contracts.

evidence.title: Sponsor: Preventing Adversaries from Developing Critical Capabilities Act (118th, H.R. 6349)
evidence.what_it_shows: Wrote a bill to block American money from funding AI and chip companies in China.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: STAR Act of 2025 (H.R. 802)
evidence.what_it_shows: Also supports tax breaks for building chip factories in America, pairing controls on China with domestic chip investment.
